title: The Flail from Heaven

full_text:
A country peasant drove two oxen to plow his field, but the horn of one ox grew so immense that it reached straight toward the sky. When the peasant could not turn the plow, he climbed up the horn and found himself walking among the clouds.

Up in the celestial heights, he saw threshers beating grain with silver flails. In the excitement of the sight, he knocked a golden flail from the sky, which plummeted back down to the earth and stuck deep into the rocky ground.

To climb down, the peasant gathered chaff and spun it into a long rope. But the rope ended far above the ground. He slid down to the very knot, hanging between heaven and earth. In his pocket, he found a small awl, cut the rope above his head, tied the cut piece below, and leaped down into the middle of a muddy pond, sinking up to his neck.

Unable to climb out of the mire, he calmly hurried home, fetched a spade from his tool shed, and dug himself out of the mud, returning home to his cottage to enjoy a pipe by the hearth, thoroughly satisfied with his grand morning excursion among the clouds.
moral: Tall tales and boundless imagination celebrate the joyful absurdity of human storytelling.

quiz.question: What is the central moral lesson taught in "The Flail from Heaven"?
options: Presence of mind and quiet wisdom triumph over brute strength.
Acting in haste and anger without thinking
Believing rumors and flattery without proof
quiz.hint: Remember the moral lesson of this traditional story.

quiz.question: How do the characters overcome their challenge?
options: Through patience, calm reflection, and wisdom
By shouting loudly and blaming others
By running away from every problem
quiz.hint: Consider the virtues praised in world folklore.

quiz.question: What memorable conclusion does this story teach young readers?
options: Honesty, kindness, and clear thinking lead to peace
quiz.hint: Reflect upon the resolution of the story.
